youtube-creators-suspicious-sponsorship-.headline: YouTube Creators - Suspicious Sponsorship Offers & Hijacks
youtube-creators-suspicious-sponsorship-.author: DANNY DE HEK
youtube-creators-suspicious-sponsorship-.core: Posted in last 7 days YouTube Creators - Suspicious Sponsorship Offers & Hijacks WARNING TO YOUTUBERS: BEWARE OF SUSPICIOUS SPONSORSHIP OFFERS I am currently investigating what appears to be a pattern of suspicious sponsorship approaches targeting YouTube content creators. Two recently registered domains have caught my attention: • fablecollab[.]com — approximately five days old. • ahacreatorproposal[.]team — approximately one month old. My Google Workspace administrator account was hijacked after I interacted with a sponsorship offer from Fable Collab. I lost access to my Google account, Gmail, YouTube Studio and other associated Google services. The attackers changed my recovery email address, removed my telephone number, added their own security key and effectively locked me out of my digital identity. Another content creator has now confidentially supplied me with correspondence from someone claiming to represent AhaCreator, using the email address partnerships@ahacreatorproposal[.]team. There are similarities between the two sponsorship approaches, including: • Personalised sponsorship offers. • Professional-looking websites and dashboards. • Attractive financial incentives. • Recognisable brands used to establish credibility. • Invitation-only access and verification procedures. • Requests to authenticate or confirm account ownership. My investigation also revealed that ahacreatorproposal[.]team redirects visitors to ahacreator[.]com. However, this does not establish who controls the newer domain or whether the correspondence is authorised. I have not established that the two operations are connected or that the companies and brands being represented are involved in fraudulent activity. Their identities could potentially be used without their knowledge or permission. I would welcome clarification from @_ahacreator regarding whether the email domain being used is officially associated with their organisation. HAS ANYONE ELSE BEEN APPROACHED? If you have received sponsorship correspondence involving Fable Collab, AhaCreator or similar creator collaboration platforms, I would like to hear from you. Please preserve the original emails, including their full technical headers. Your identity can remain confidential. In the meantime, I strongly recommend that content creators take the following precautions: • Do not click unfamiliar sponsorship links. • Independently verify the sender and sponsorship agency. • Do not authenticate using Google through unfamiliar websites. • Never disclose Google backup codes or verification codes. • Do not download unfamiliar sponsorship documents or software. The image accompanying this post shows the personalised sponsorship offer that preceded the takeover of my Google account. These offers can look incredibly professional and convincing. Recognisable brands, personalised information and attractive financial incentives can all contribute to a false sense of security. A few hundred dollars in sponsorship revenue is not worth risking years of hard work and access to your entire digital identity. Please share this warning with other content creators. I would rather raise awareness now than wait until another YouTuber becomes a victim. #YouTube #Phishing #CyberSecurity #AccountHijacking #SponsorshipScam #ContentCreators #OnlineSafety

writers-and-photographers-in-nigeria-ove.headline: Writers & Photographers in Nigeria - Overlooked Community Stories
writers-and-photographers-in-nigeria-ove.author: Quareeb  Jagun
writers-and-photographers-in-nigeria-ove.core: Posted in last 7 days Writers & Photographers in Nigeria - Overlooked Community Stories People who don't record their own experience are going to have someone else write their story. In our communities there are people whose lives are worth recording, traditions whose history needs to be preserved and young people out there doing real work who are never acknowledged. Yet quite often those experiences don't get into the stories we tell about ourselves. This is one of the reasons why I have continued to write, to research and to tell the stories of Africa, of its people, of its history and of its everyday life. Storytelling should do more than just entertain. It should be about preserving memory, challenging the way we see things and helping us to understand each other. Today I'm pleased to announce my appointment as Country Ambassador for EL Lente Humano (The Human Lens) which is an international storytelling initiative based in Mexico. This is a chance to get to know people, to find out about experiences that are otherwise overlooked, to record our cultural heritage and to provide space for more voices to be heard. I hope to build links with Nigerian writers, historians, researchers, photographers, the younger generation and community storytellers and to link their work to audiences across Africa and the world. But I'd like to start with a question. Who in your circle actually deserves to have their story told? It could be a Granny going the extra mile to keep an old tradition alive, it could be a young person doing something to effect change in their own community, it could be a local historian doing their bit to preserve our shared memory, or it could be someone whose life story has a lot to teach us. I want to hear about them. I want to get to know you. I want us to record these experiences in a way that is honest, with dignity and with respect. Africa has always had stories. We just need to be more deliberate about finding them, recording them and sharing them with the world. Let's not wait until these stories become history before we realise they were worth recording. Special thanks to Jana Gaia Romero, for the trust, the confidence and the opportunity to be part of this mission. If you're a writer, a storyteller, a photographer, a researcher, a young changemaker or indeed just someone with a story they'd like to share then I'd be very interested in getting in touch. Let's tell our stories together. Jagun Quareeb Alabi Nigeria Country Ambassador The Human Lens +2349046463436 #TheHumanLens #AfricanStorytelling #Nigeria #PanAfricanism #Storytelling

hospital-ceos-and-cfos-and-rev-cycle-hea.headline: Hospital CEOs & CFOs & Rev Cycle Heads - 14-Day Full Payment Tradeoff
hospital-ceos-and-cfos-and-rev-cycle-hea.author: Ben Phillips
hospital-ceos-and-cfos-and-rev-cycle-hea.core: Posted in last 7 days Hospital CEOs & CFOs & Rev Cycle Heads - 14-Day Full Payment Tradeoff Your hospital contract says 250% of Medicare. What actually hits your bank account? And how long does it take to get there? Kodiak’s 2025 provider data showed an average of 55 days to insurance payment. Providers collected just 42% of the dollars patients owed. So here’s my question for hospital CEOs, CFOs, and the people who run payer contracting and revenue cycle. Would you take a lower contracted rate if you got 100% of the agreed amount in 7 to 14 days, including the patient’s deductible, copay, and coinsurance? Say a contract pays 250% of Medicare on paper, but after final denials, downcoding, underpayments, and unpaid patient balances, you actually collect 175%. That’s a hypothetical. If those were your numbers, would you sign at 185% for the same services if the full payment hit your account within 14 days of claim acceptance and your team never had to chase the patient balance? I run an independent physician association, and I want to hear from the hospital CEOs, CFOs, and leaders who oversee payer contracting, billing, and revenue cycle. Across your hospital, all in: 1. For every $100 you expect to collect, how much actually comes in? 2. How long does it take, and how many patients end up in collections? 3. What rate would you sign for if you could count on the full payment within 14 days? If the numbers are sensitive, DM me. A rough range is enough. I cover healthcare payment, cost, and access on Healthcare Uncut. Subscribe on YouTube or Spotify, and get the weekly schedule in The CEO Brief. https://lnkd.in/g8sUkD29

researchers-and-founders-under-35-2027-i.core: Posted in last 7 days Researchers & Founders Under 35 - 2027 Innovators Nominations Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open https://ift.tt/hc0yn91 Every year, the editors at MIT Technology Review select 35 of the world’s top young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors to honor as our newest class of Innovators Under 35. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations. We’re on the hunt for researchers and founders who are engineering solutions to some of the most formidable problems society faces, including human disease and climate change. We also recognize those who have made clever and useful inventions, important new scientific discoveries, or technological breakthroughs early in their careers. We want to hear about people, based anywhere in the world, who are responsible for a major finding or advance and can show real-world impact from their work. To qualify for the list, a nominee must be under the age of 35 as of October 1, 2027 (that is, born on or after October 2, 1992). Have someone in mind?
